guardrail: Research is hypothesis generation only. No item in this file is allowed to change live predictions until separately validated.
research_summary: Evidence supports conditioning short-horizon momentum on liquidity, volume, volatility, time of day, and information intensity rather than treating continuation as unconditional. Trading-volume/return dynamics distinguish continuation from reversal, while liquidity and volatility affect reversal speed and persistence. Motif discovery and change-point methods provide leakage-safe ways to search for unnamed structures. ([nber.org](https://www.nber.org/papers/w30917?utm_source=openai))

hypotheses.title: Impulse exhaustion and bounce decay
hypotheses.claim: After a large intraday impulse, successive pullback bounces have declining median size and increasing failure probability, especially when each bounce forms a lower high.
hypotheses.why_it_might_matter: Separates temporary reflex rallies from renewed information-driven demand; longer runs can precede larger reversals. ([nber.org](https://www.nber.org/papers/w14160?utm_source=openai))
hypotheses.target_outcome: Forward 5-minute and 30-minute return, probability of a 5% or 10% drawdown, and minutes until drawdown.
hypotheses.expected_direction: Larger impulse, weaker relative volume, smaller later bounces, and lower highs should predict weaker forward returns and faster failure.
hypotheses.recommended_test: Event study with sequential bounce labeling; use stock-day clustered confidence intervals and walk-forward threshold selection.
hypotheses.minimum_evidence_to_promote: Out-of-sample monotonicity across at least three market regimes, economically meaningful effect after spread/slippage, and bootstrap confidence excluding zero.
hypotheses.failure_or_rejection_criteria: No monotonic bounce decay, instability across price/float buckets, or disappearance after controlling for volatility and time of day.
hypotheses.promotion_gate: Must be implemented as a leakage-safe historical experiment and pass out-of-sample / walk-forward validation before use.

hypotheses.title: VWAP reclaim quality
hypotheses.claim: A pullback that reclaims VWAP with expanding relative volume and holds above it for multiple bars has a higher probability of making a new intraday high than a brief low-volume reclaim.
hypotheses.why_it_might_matter: VWAP deviation and intraday volume share are measurable proxies for trend versus mean-reversion conditions. ([papers.ssrn.com](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=2363483&utm_source=openai))
hypotheses.target_outcome: New-high occurrence within 15 and 30 minutes, maximum favorable excursion, and failure-to-VWAP probability.
hypotheses.expected_direction: Sustained reclaim plus volume expansion should increase continuation odds; low-volume reclaim should predict failure or mean reversion.
hypotheses.recommended_test: Matched event study comparing reclaims with propensity matching on impulse size, time, volatility, and liquidity; validate chronologically.
hypotheses.minimum_evidence_to_promote: At least 10 percentage-point improvement in new-high probability or statistically robust positive net excursion in independent periods.
hypotheses.failure_or_rejection_criteria: Effect vanishes after spread, volume, and time-of-day controls or exists only in one catalyst subgroup.
hypotheses.promotion_gate: Must be implemented as a leakage-safe historical experiment and pass out-of-sample / walk-forward validation before use.

hypotheses.title: Climax volume versus informed continuation
hypotheses.claim: Volume climax followed by price progress failure predicts reversal, while high volume accompanied by continued directional progress predicts continuation; the distinction is stronger in liquid names.
hypotheses.why_it_might_matter: Research finds speculative/information-related volume is more continuation-prone, while other trading motives are more reversal-prone. ([nber.org](https://www.nber.org/papers/w8312?utm_source=openai))
hypotheses.target_outcome: Forward directional return, 5%/10% drawdown probability, and time-to-failure after the climax.
hypotheses.expected_direction: High volume with poor price progress and widening spreads should predict exhaustion; high volume with efficient price progress should predict continuation.
hypotheses.recommended_test: Cross-sectional intraday event study with volume-climax definitions fixed in prior training windows; use out-of-sample deciles and turnover-adjusted outcomes.
hypotheses.minimum_evidence_to_promote: Stable separation between top and bottom signal quintiles across multiple years and liquidity buckets after realistic execution costs.
hypotheses.failure_or_rejection_criteria: No separation in forward returns, unstable sign, or signal explained entirely by contemporaneous volatility.
hypotheses.promotion_gate: Must be implemented as a leakage-safe historical experiment and pass out-of-sample / walk-forward validation before use.

hypotheses.title: Late-session continuation versus exhaustion
hypotheses.claim: Late-session strength is more likely to carry into the next session or final half-hour when supported by persistent relative volume and higher closes, but late weak bounces after lower highs have elevated same-day failure risk.
hypotheses.why_it_might_matter: Recent evidence reports cross-day momentum concentrated in the last half-hour, while momentum can also experience sharp crashes and reversals. ([papers.ssrn.com](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=4934543&utm_source=openai))
hypotheses.target_outcome: Final-hour continuation, closing-price breakout, next-session gap direction, and 5%/10% post-signal drawdown.
hypotheses.expected_direction: Persistent late strength should improve continuation odds; weak late bounces after failed reclaims should predict rapid failure and larger drawdowns.
hypotheses.recommended_test: Separate same-session and next-session event studies; train on earlier dates and test on later dates with session-level clustering.
hypotheses.minimum_evidence_to_promote: Positive effect in both same-session and at least one later-period holdout, with drawdown estimates stable across catalyst types.
hypotheses.failure_or_rejection_criteria: Effect is limited to opening/closing auction artifacts, disappears using executable prices, or reverses across years.
hypotheses.promotion_gate: Must be implemented as a leakage-safe historical experiment and pass out-of-sample / walk-forward validation before use.

hypotheses.title: Step-plateau-reacceleration structure
hypotheses.claim: A multi-session pattern of upward step, higher-level price acceptance, declining realized volatility, and renewed volume expansion predicts a higher probability of fresh multi-session highs than a similar-looking one-session spike.
hypotheses.why_it_might_matter: Separating accepted repricing from transient spikes may improve catalyst-driven continuation classification and reduce false breakout signals.
hypotheses.target_outcome: New 5-session high, 3-session excess return, maximum drawdown, and time-to-failure.
hypotheses.expected_direction: Higher lows, retained gaps, compressed plateau volatility, and renewed volume should predict stronger continuation; rapid rejection into the plateau should predict failure.
hypotheses.recommended_test: Define states using only historical data, estimate transition probabilities in rolling training windows, and evaluate on later untouched sessions.
hypotheses.minimum_evidence_to_promote: Positive out-of-sample hazard ratio for new highs and improved precision over simple breakout/return baselines across at least two holdout periods.
hypotheses.failure_or_rejection_criteria: No improvement over momentum and volatility baselines, or performance depends on hindsight-defined plateau boundaries.
hypotheses.promotion_gate: Must be implemented as a leakage-safe historical experiment and pass out-of-sample / walk-forward validation before use.

hypotheses.title: Unsupervised motif and regime discovery
hypotheses.claim: Leakage-safe clustering of normalized price-volume-microstructure sequences will identify recurring unnamed motifs with stable, distinct forward outcomes beyond manually specified setups.
hypotheses.why_it_might_matter: Motif methods can discover repeated subsequences without predefining pattern length or trading terminology, but discovery and validation must be separated chronologically. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1006.1526?utm_source=openai))
hypotheses.target_outcome: Forward 5-, 15-, and 30-minute returns, new-high probability, 5%/10% drawdown risk, and time-to-failure.
hypotheses.expected_direction: Some motifs should show persistent, economically interpretable outcome differences after controlling for common factors; most discovered motifs should fail replication.
hypotheses.recommended_test: Use rolling historical windows for motif discovery, freeze motifs and labels, then test only on later dates; require nested validation, purging, embargoes, and false-discovery correction.
hypotheses.minimum_evidence_to_promote: Replication in multiple unseen chronological blocks, effect surviving transaction costs and simple baselines, and no dependence on a single ticker or event.
hypotheses.failure_or_rejection_criteria: Performance collapses under purged validation, motif definitions drift materially, or discovered clusters lack stable forward outcome separation.
hypotheses.promotion_gate: Must be implemented as a leakage-safe historical experiment and pass out-of-sample / walk-forward validation before use.

important_caveats: Intraday results are highly sensitive to quote/trade cleaning, split adjustments, halts, borrow constraints, and executable spread assumptions.
Catalyst labels, float, short interest, and news timestamps can contain revision or availability bias; use point-in-time snapshots.
Low-priced small-cap stocks create severe selection, survivorship, delisting, and market-impact biases.
Use purged walk-forward validation, date-based holdouts, embargo periods, and nested feature selection to prevent leakage.
Report conditional distributions, not only mean returns; 5% and 10% drawdowns may be driven by a small number of extreme events.
A statistically significant pattern is not production-ready without capacity, turnover, latency, and implementation-cost analysis.
research_gaps: Reliable point-in-time datasets linking catalyst novelty, float changes, halts, borrow conditions, and intraday order-book data.
Formal estimation of second- and third-bounce failure hazards by liquidity and catalyst class.
Whether VWAP reclaim quality remains predictive after controlling for order-flow imbalance and market-wide intraday regimes.
How motif stability changes across regulatory periods, market-structure changes, and retail-participation regimes.
Comparisons of matrix-profile, shapelet, HMM, change-point, and contrastive representation methods under identical purged walk-forward tests.
